findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed multiple items (sandwiches and cut vegetables) in the double door standing cooler nearest the cafeteria to be without date marking. When the inspector asked the date the items were prepped it was stated that the items were prepared on Tuesday (09/02). CORRECTED- the person in charge (PIC) placed dates on the items. Food being cold held for more than 24 hours must be used or discarded within seven days. Date marking helps to prevent foods from being held past an unsafe date. Educate all employees about date marking requirements.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the two dish plates in the facility to not be operational. The PIC has communicated with maintenance to obtain new batteries for the temperature measuring devices. Inspector will return on 09/15/25 to check that the batteries in both heat plates have been replaced, and both devices are working. When a facility is using heat for sanitation purposes there must be heat detection plates. Facility should use plates on a regular basis to ensure the proper sanitizing temperature is being reached (160F+).
findings.citation_text: 4-302.13(A) Temperature Measuring Devices, Manual and Mechanical Warewashing. (A) In manual WAREWASHING operations, a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be provided and readily accessible for frequently measuring the washing and SANITIZING temperatures. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
No ambient thermometers were observed inside the coolers throughout the kitchen. Ensure ambient thermometers are placed in any cold cooler that holds TCS foods.
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Sanitizer bucket observed with a quat concentration of 100ppm. CORRECTED- Upon request, employee remade sanitizer bucket. Sanitizer observed at 400ppm quat.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have concentration based on label (200-400ppm). [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
Final rinse temperature dial on the dish machine is not functional. Dial remains pointing at 80-90F regardless of actual rinse temperature as measured by a plate type dishwasher thermometer. 
4-204.115: A WAREWASHING machine shall be equipped with a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that indicates the temperature of the water: (A) In each wash and rinse tank; (B) As the water enters the hot water SANITIZING final rinse manifold or in the chemical SANITIZING solution tank. [Pf]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Employee doing salad bar prep was observed using the handwashing sink at the end of the service line to wash produce. Proper use of handwashing sinks and washing produce at the prep sink were discussed. Produce was taken to prep sink to be washed prior to prep.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using handwashing sinks for other purposes.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Sani-buckets were observed with concentration below 100ppm quat while the 3 part sink was observed at proper concentration of 200ppm quat. Sani-buckets were prepared for use upon arrival of staff and were used to wipe down tables prior to arrival of inspector. Concentration was worn down from use. Fresh sanitizer solutions were provided at 200ppm. Ensure solutions are changed frequently/between uses as needed throughout the day and maintained at proper concentration.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11 Employee was observed at the 3 part sink quickly dunking a knife in sanitizer solution prior to setting it aside to air dry during ware washing. Proper contact time of at least 30 seconds was discussed. Knife was placed back in the sanitizer solution to allow for proper contact time during sanitization. 
After being cleaned, equipment food contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in chemical manual operations, including the application of sanitizing chemicals by immersion, manual swabbing, brushing, or pressure spraying methods, using a solution as specified under § 4-501.114 (in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions). Contact time shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use instructions by providing at least 30 seconds for quaternary ammonia chemical sanitizing solutions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Portions of cheese shreds were observed in a large pan at the service line where salad bar prep was underway. Cheese shreds were observed at 54F-57F. Cheese shreds were portioned the Friday prior and were pulled from the cooler this morning to be further portioned into a smaller container for use during lunch. Prep was occurring in the 9 o’clock hour, and salad bar would not be set up until closer to 10:40am. Cheese shreds were placed in a freezer to quickly drop the temperature prior to storing in the cooler until closer to time for service. PIC was advised to have staff get out only what they need as they are working on prep to limit time TCS foods spend in the temperature danger zone.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Sani-buckets were observed with concentration of 0ppm quat while the 3 part sink was observed at proper concentration of 200ppm quat. Sanitizer container connected to the dispenser was less than a quarter full and air bubbles were observed in the suction line. A new sanitizer container was connected to the dispenser, and freshly dispensed solutions in the sani-buckets were observed at 200ppm. Kitchen staff were advised to allow the dispenser to run for several seconds prior to filling buckets and the 3 part sink to allow proper suction and removal of air bubbles that may interfere with product flow and to verify proper concentration with quat test strips.    
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 One of the food employees working at the time of inspection did not have a signed reporting agreement on file. The employee was hired as of November 2019. Kitchen manager had the employee go over the health policy and sign a copy of the reporting agreement during the inspection. All other staff working at the time, including the kitchen manager, had signed reporting agreements on file. Additional copies of the reporting agreement were provided. Ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy upon hiring, and maintain signed copies of reporting agreements for all staff. 
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.13 Food employee handled a cell phone and personal beverage and did not wash hands prior to going to the dish area to handle and put away clean dishes. Handwashing between tasks was discussed. Employee immediately washed hands with proper technique prior to continuing with the task. 
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in any activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Worker was observed scratching her head around the edge of her hairnet and did not wash hands prior to handling clean dishes. Handwashing was discussed; manager was advised to reiterate when to wash hands with all staff. 
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands and after touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Slight accumulation of pink mold was observed on the baffle inside the ice machine. Manager stated it had been a couple weeks since the baffle was cleaned. Cleaning frequency of the ice machine was discussed. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
NOTE: Make sure the ceiling inside the machine behind the baffle and the components lithe ice tray/filter area are getting cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-901.11 Cleaned and sanitized dishes were observed being wiped down with a wiping cloth. Staff were advised on proper/complete air drying prior to storing cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils. 
After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility does not have a way to verify the surface temperature of dishes if the digital readout is questionable. Options for measuring the final rinse temperature were discussed. Manager was asked to email inspector with final decision on product that will be purchased and used for checking the surface temperature of final rinse in the dish machine.
In hot water mechanical ware washing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 (E)(4) Ceiling inside the ice machine behind the baffle was soiled with mold. It appeared to be mostly soiled around the shoot where ice comes out but may also have some accumulation up inside the shoot. Mold accumulation may also be present in the upper compartment where the filter and ice tray are located. Manager was advised to work with custodial staff and/or outside company (whoever would be responsible for detail cleaning) to get all the components of the ice machine properly cleaned and sanitized. (see general comments for additional information)

Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Cheese sauce in the warmer was observed with an internal temperature of 118°F. Staff noted the final cook temperature was 170°F prior to some cold cheese product getting added just before placing product in the warmer. Some of the cold cheese pieces were still in the process of melting and were likely the reason the cheese sauce was below 135°F. Cheese sauce was placed back on the stove to reheat to 165°F prior to mixing with cooked noodles for service. Staff were advised to make sure foods are at proper cook temperature prior to placing in the warmer, especially after cold ingredients are added to cooked product. 

Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Mouse droppings were observed on the floor in the dry storage room used for school food service supplies. The majority of the droppings were in the corner under canned good storage. Clean the floor in the dry storage room (see general comments for additional information)

Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - A slight buildup of pink mold was observed on the lower portion of the white baffle inside the ice machine. Last cleaning of the baffle likely occurred prior to spring break. 

Clean and sanitize the baffle in the ice machine as needed to eliminate buildup of mold and minimize the risk of potential cross contamination.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.530 - Employee was observed chewing gum in the kitchen. Employee discarded the gum per inspector's request.

Employees shall consume food, including gum and candy, only in designated dining areas. An employee dining area shall not be so designated if consuming food there may result in contamination of other food, equipment, utensils, or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Pre-flushed, scraped, soaked
findings.citation_text:
750.830 - Pot hanging in clean storage area above the 3 part sink had food debris stuck on the outer surface. Pan was removed to go through ware washing process again.

Equipment and utensils shall be pre-flushed or pre-scraped and, when necessary, pre-soaked to remove gross food particles and soil prior to their being cleaned in a dishwashing machine unless a pre-wash cycle is a part of the dishwashing machine operation. If food debris or general soil remains, then repeat the process as many times as necessary to ensure all surfaces are free of stuck on debris and properly cleaned and sanitized.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 - Employee had bare hand contact with the roller on the side of the dispenser to retrieve paper towels once hands were already washed. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Employee was advised to have paper towels ready to dry hands prior to beginning handwashing process. If any general surfaces (faucet handle, paper towel dispenser handle, etc.) are touched during the process without a barrier for any reason then handwashing should occur again with the proper technique and use of barriers to avoid re-contamination of freshly washed hands.

Employees shall properly wash hands any time hands may be been contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
750.650a - A) Plastic ice scoop was observed with a crack along the top edge. Replace the scoop.

B) Small cutting board used for slicing citrus on service line was observed with pits and discoloration. Cutting board may be sanded to see if the board can be resurfaced and kept for use a little longer. If sanding doesn't allow for cleaning and sanitizing to remove discoloration, then replace the cutting board.

 Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.citation_text:
750.690 - Rust accumulation was observed in the bottom of the milk cooler that was located next to the Pepsi cooler. The bottom inside the milk cooler was rough to the touch. See about repairing or replacing the cooler. All surfaces need to be smooth and easily cleanable.

Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - Pink mold accumulation was observed on the white baffle in the ice machine. Clean and sanitize the baffle as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. 

Clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed, up to every 4hrs after continuous use (i.e. knives, cutting boards, etc.). to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floors were observed to be soiled with food and/or general buildup under the steam table on the service line and in the dish area along the walls/in corners under the dish machine and the clean equipment storage shelving. Clean the floors in the aforementioned areas.

Floors shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Observed wet wiping cloths stored on the counter. Cloths were used to wipe off shredded cheese spill. Cloths were moved to the used linen basket during the inspection. keep a sani-bucket available for these cloths. Have one bucket for non-food contact (tables) and one for food contact. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.citation_text:
750.250 - Mac-n-cheese in the steam table had an internal temperature of 118F. Staff stated the noodles were boiled and then combined with milk and butter (from cooler) and cheese sauce (from dry storage) to make the final product. Adding cold and ambient temperature products to the boiled noodles may have dropped the temperature below the minimum hot holding temperature. Staff also noted the holding well in question sometimes has difficulty maintaining proper temperature. Mac-n-cheese was reheated to 165F prior to being placed back in the steam table (in the middle holding well).

All hot potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 135F/above while on display and service.
**When combining ingredients at various temperatures (cooked versus cold, etc.) make sure the temperature of a hot product does not drop below 135F. If it does, then reheat to 165F/above prior to placing foods in hot holding equipment for service**

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.citation_text:
750.1220 - Floor under steam table at hot service line and the floor drain were soiled with buildup of food and general debris. Clean the floor and the drain under the hot service line as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

Floors and drains shall be maintained clean.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed overhead debris to have fallen onto one of the ice scoops in the holder over the ice machine. During the inspection, the ice scoop was removed and brought to the dish room for proper cleaning. Watch that scoops are clean prior to use. Area over scoop is currently observed clean. To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment: 750-240 Observed a frozen bag thawing in a sink without water running. During the inspection, water was run over the thawing food. Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Observed the floors throughout to be soiled along the floor-to-wall area (soiled with grease and dust). Make sure the floors get scrubbed and the pest traps around the walls get replaced as needed (some were observed dusty). Also, the floor drains need to have the grates removed and the basins scrubbed. Floor drains observed soiled with mold and food accumulation. Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Floors throughout are clean. The coving in the dish room and the dry storage is soiled. Make sure that when sweeping the soil isn't forced into the wall-to-floor crevices.  Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 REPEAT: The wall behind the reach-in milk cooler is damaged from the door banging the wall. Seal the wall and provide a permanent solution to eliminate the damage (Plexi-glass or plastic bumper).  All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment: 750-830g See notes from previous inspection report. The dishmachine digital display does not indicate the rinse temperature. The display reads properly through the wash cycle and then falls to 0 - 77F during the rinse cycle. Inspector ran through an indicating strip and determined temperature to be above 180F. Provide a properly reading digital display OR provide test strips appropriate for the heat sanitizing machine. A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Wet wiping cloths were observed by the 3-part sink and on the counters. Provide a proper sani-bucket for the wet cloths. Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1060 The drainline of the 3-part sink has a minor leak around the second connection. Water leaks are observed ponding along the wall of the sink.  All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 REPEAT: The wall behind the milk cooler in the cafe continues to have chipping paint/drywall. Seal the wall and provide a bumper to protect the wall from the hinged-lid of the milk cooler. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
